market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner or operations manager of a powder coating / plating / heat-treating service bureau (5–60 employees). Often owner-operator family business; in larger shops, ops manager drives software selection with owner sign-off.
market_sizing.business_count_au: IBISWorld 'Metal Coating and Finishing in Australia' (ANZSIC 2243) reports ~1,266 businesses in 2025 (declining ~2.6% CAGR 2020–2025), industry size AUD ~2.1bn. Powder coating is the largest single sub-segment within this — credible estimate is 700–900 dedicated powder coating shops + ~200–300 plating/anodising/heat-treat bureaus. Total addressable: ~900–1,200 process-step service bureaus.
market_sizing.business_count_global: US: ~5,000+ custom coaters (PCI/CCAI membership and Custom Coaters directory). UK: ~600–800. Canada: ~500. Global SMB process-finishing TAM: 30,000–50,000 shops (including plating, heat-treat, anodising, painting). Steelhead's TAM pitch references >25,000 finishing job shops in NA alone.
market_sizing.typical_size: 5–40 employees, AUD 800k–10m revenue. Most AU shops are 8–25 staff with AUD 2m–6m revenue.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: Steelhead Technologies (process-manufacturing native): from USD 500/mo entry; mid deployments USD 1.5k–4k/mo. PaintShop Pro Manager / Sherwin-Williams Coatings.AI tools: bundled / undisclosed. Generic shop floor tools (Fishbowl, Katana, Cin7) AUD 99–500/mo but don't model batch/rack/recipe workflows. Heavy-tier (Plex, IQMS, SYSPRO) start USD 3k–5k/mo. Many AU shops still run Excel + Xero/MYOB + handwritten batch tickets — no incumbent in the AUD 200–500/mo band designed for the workflow.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AUD 200–500/mo for entry, AUD 600–1,200/mo at 20+ staff with multiple lines. Owners are price-sensitive but pain is acute (Nadcap audits, AS9100 traceability for aerospace work, customer cert demands). Steelhead's traction at USD 500/mo+ proves willingness. AU-adjusted: AUD 350/mo blended is realistic.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Inside sales + free pilot + word-of-mouth in tight industry. Many shops know each other regionally; one good reference unlocks 3–5 prospects. Trade-show demos (AISF events) drive trial signups. Self-serve is feasible for entry tier but >AUD 500/mo wants a demo call.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: AUD 350–500/mo blended. Entry AUD 249/mo (single line, <10 staff), mid AUD 549/mo (2–3 lines, batch/recipe), enterprise AUD 1,200+/mo (multi-line, Nadcap, customer portal).
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong. (1) Per-line / per-station pricing scales with shop. (2) Customer portal as paid add-on (customers track their own racks/jobs). (3) Embedded payments on customer invoices. (4) Certificate-of-conformity generation as premium feature (Nadcap shops will pay). (5) Powder/chemical inventory + supplier rebate marketplace (Dulux Powders, Akzo Nobel, Prismatic). (6) AI vision QA (powder coverage / film thickness) is a credible USD 200–400/mo upsell. 2–3× ARPU expansion realistic.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) **Steelhead Technologies** — clear category leader, founded specifically for finishing/heat-treat/plating shops; just raised USD 84m growth from Mainsail (Dec 2025), prior USD 12.5m Series B (2024). Models recipes, racks, customer-owned inventory, traceability, Nadcap Scanner hardware add-on. Strong US footprint, growing internationally but minimal AU presence today. 2) **MetalTrace / Metaltrace ERP** — niche heat-treat focus, smaller. 3) **PaintShop Manager** (US/UK, older) — desktop-era tool. 4) **PowderTrack / Powdershop tools** — fragmented small vendors. 5) Generic ERPs (Fishbowl, Katana, Cin7, MYOB Acumatica) — not built for batch/rack/recipe workflow. 6) AU-specific: nothing dominant; Jobman has powder coating customers but is timber-leaning. **Steelhead is the only credible vertical incumbent and they're under-penetrated in AU/NZ.**
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: Steelhead is 6 years old (founded ~2019). Older niche tools (PaintShop, MetalTrace) date to 2000s but have small footprints. The category is unusually young — no 30-year-old legacy dominant player. This is both opportunity (segment is software-naïve) and threat (Steelhead is well-funded and modern).
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Steelhead enjoys generally positive reviews on Capterra/G2 (4.5+ stars), case studies highlight 'parts not paper' framing. Common complaint pattern from non-Steelhead shops: 'we still run on Excel and handwritten travellers', 'our ERP doesn't understand racks or recipes', 'customer keeps asking for certs we have to manually compile'. PCI/CCAI forums and AISF chatter focus on labour shortage and compliance burden more than software dissatisfaction — because most shops haven't yet adopted vertical software at all. The gap is **lack of adoption**, not dissatisfaction with an existing tool.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Major: Steelhead — USD 84m growth investment from Mainsail Partners (Dec 2025). This was the largest single round in the finishing/job-shop SaaS category. No other meaningful AU-relevant raises in 2025–26. Mainsail's involvement signals expectation of category roll-up and international expansion — a competing AU/NZ-focused entrant has a 12–24 month window before Steelhead localises.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Rising. Steelhead is investing heavily post-raise in AI scheduling, vision-based QA, and automation. Independent AI quoting startups (Phasio for additive, AutoQuote3D) hint at adjacent moves. AI-vision for film-thickness / coverage QA is the obvious next wave. Window for a generic AI play is closing; a localised AU product with AI add-ons is still viable.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: **Batch tickets, recipe management, and customer-owned inventory** are unsolved. A typical shop receives a customer's parts (customer owns the inventory, not the shop), assigns them to a rack, selects a powder recipe (e.g. Dulux Electro Topcoat, 200°C 20min, two coats), runs the batch through pre-treat → coat → cure → QC, generates a certificate of conformity, and ships back. Today this lives on paper job cards or Excel: lost cards = lost parts, recipe drift = rework, no easy trace from 'this rack on Tuesday' to 'this customer's PO and cert'. Customer portals for tracking are essentially non-existent in AU. Nadcap audits require 7+ year traceability that's reconstructed from paper.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: (1) Customer-owned inventory and rack-level traceability is a hard, domain-specific data model — competitors can't paper over it. (2) Recipe library (with supplier powder SKUs from Dulux, Akzo Nobel, Prismatic, Interpon) accumulates value. (3) AISF / industry-body relationships and certifications. (4) Nadcap / AS9100 cert templates — once shops trust your audit trail, switching is risky. (5) Embedded payments + supplier marketplace.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Must-have: Xero, MYOB, Stripe, label/QR printers (Brother/Zebra), email/PDF. Important: powder supplier catalogues (Dulux Powders, Interpon, Prismatic Australia), ABN Lookup, MSDS/SDS document storage. Nice-to-have: oven controller integrations (Eurotherm — relevant for AMS2750/Nadcap heat treaters), temperature data loggers, customer-portal SSO.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Very low. Most AU shops have no vertical software at all — direct rip-and-replace of paper/Excel is the dominant scenario. A minority have Fishbowl or generic accounting + light job tracking, but switching cost is minimal.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Moderate-to-high depending on customer mix. Generic powder coating: ISO 9001 + customer-specific QA. Architectural (Dulux Duralloy/Duratec): Qualicoat / AAMA-style accreditation, film thickness/adhesion testing. Aerospace heat-treat/plating: Nadcap AC7102 (heat-treat), AC7108 (chem processing) — requires extensive process control, calibration records, AMS2750 furnace pyrometry, 7–20 year record retention. Plating: hexavalent chrome / RoHS / REACH chemical reporting. WHS spray-booth and confined-space requirements (state-level).
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: (1) **PFAS phase-out** — AU is implementing PFAS restrictions through 2025–2026 affecting some plating/finishing chemistries; record-keeping for chemical use is increasing. (2) **AASB S2 climate-related financial disclosures** — Scope 1/2 emissions reporting from large customers will cascade to finishing suppliers (oven gas, electricity); shops will be asked to report emissions per job/batch by 2027 — software that captures this is a wedge. (3) **Modern Slavery** and supply-chain due-diligence reporting widening. (4) Nadcap AC7102 / AC7108 periodic revisions (typical 3-year cycle, next ~2026). (5) State-level EPA tightening on VOC emissions and chrome/cyanide handling. None are individually catastrophic forcing functions like NDIS Support at Home, but cumulative compliance overhead is real and pushes shops toward digital systems.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: High. Finishing is a process industry — recipes, racks, batches, cures, customer-owned inventory, and Nadcap nuance are non-obvious to outsiders. 6–12 months of immersive learning (shop visits, AISF events, talking to platers + heat-treaters) is the minimum. Founder fit (Manuva) provides general manufacturing literacy but not finishing-specific depth.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 6–9 months for a credible v1 (batch ticket → rack → recipe → cert → invoice + Xero sync). 9–12 months to add Nadcap-grade traceability and oven data integration.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: (1) Recipe + batch state machine is fiddly but well-defined. (2) Oven/controller integrations (Eurotherm, Honeywell) for heat-treat shops — non-trivial; can be deferred to v2. (3) Customer-portal SSO + customer-owned inventory logic is a meaningful schema shift but solvable. (4) Optional AI vision QA (film thickness, coverage) — depends on hardware partnership. No truly hard ML problems for MVP.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Moderate. State EPAs differ on VOC, chrome, cyanide and waste reporting (e.g. VIC EPA vs NSW EPA), and WHS regs vary; mostly handled as configurable compliance templates, not separate rule engines.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Not strictly required for general finishing. Defence/aerospace customers may require AU-hosted data; Supabase Sydney covers this. Not a blocker.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: (1) **AISF (Australasian Institute of Surface Finishing)** — peak body for anodisers, electroplaters, powder coaters, plus suppliers. Annual conference, regional events, training. Sponsorship and speaking slots are accessible to startups. (2) **SCAA (Surface Coatings Association Australia)** — broader coatings, mostly paint chemists but useful adjacency. (3) **Powder supplier reseller networks** — Dulux Powders, Interpon (AkzoNobel), Prismatic Australia all maintain shop relationships and can be referral partners. (4) **Cold outbound** — shops are public B2B; AISF member directory + Custom Coaters directory + ABN Lookup yields a clean target list of <1,500 shops nationally. (5) **Trade shows** — AusTech, Australian Manufacturing Week, AISF Annual Conference. (6) **Content/SEO** — 'powder coating software AU', 'Nadcap heat treat software', 'job traveller batch ticket' are winnable. (7) Limited Facebook community; not a primary channel.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 2–4 directly relevant: AISF (primary), SCAA, ASI (steel), AMTIL (broader manufacturing).
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: ~3–5: AISF newsletter, Australian Paint Magazine, Surface Engineering International, AMT magazine (AMTIL), Manufacturers' Monthly.
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Small. Powder coating groups (global) have ~10k–30k members but AU-specific groups are <5k. Not the primary channel.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2–4 sub-$10k options annually: AISF Annual Conference, AusTech, AMW state expos, state-level AISF meetings.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High. Shops are publicly listed, AISF + Custom Coaters directories are scrapable, owners answer the phone. Total target list ~1,000–1,500 shops — small enough that founder-led outreach can cover the whole TAM in 12–18 months.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Moderate. Powder coating culture is tight-knit, family-business, slightly skeptical of tech vendors but warm to peers who 'speak shop'. An outsider needs to invest in AISF presence, shop visits, and ideally hire a domain-expert advisor (ex-shop foreman) early. Easier than vet or funeral, harder than generic fab.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate. First 5 paying references probably require visiting 30–50 shops, AISF event attendance, and 3–6 month free pilots. Maybe 4–7 months focused effort.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Low-to-moderate. Highly specific keywords (Qualicoat, AMS2750, Nadcap AC7102, batch ticket software) have low volume but low competition; AU-localised content is wide open. Generic 'powder coating software' is dominated by Steelhead.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Mostly none. Optional: Qualicoat / AAMA / Nadcap auditors may want export formats; achievable. Powder suppliers (Dulux, Interpon) hold pricing data but are partners, not gatekeepers.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~50–60%. Direct reuse: tenants, RLS, users/roles, suppliers, items, locations, activity_log, invoicing. New: customer-owned inventory model, racks, batches, recipes, ovens/lines, certificates of conformity, Nadcap audit trail tables. The shift from 'we own the materials and make products' to 'customer owns the parts and we apply a process' is a meaningful schema change.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: High. Next.js + Supabase + RLS + tenant context + design system + Xero/MYOB integration patterns + invite/auth all transfer cleanly.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Low. Powder coaters and plating bureaus are distinct from Manuva's MTS manufacturers. Limited cross-sell. Mostly a fresh GTM and brand.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Adjacent but distinct. Same shop-floor mental model, different process metaphor (service-on-customer-parts vs make-to-stock).
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12–18 months. Steelhead is the real competitive threat but is busy expanding in the US post-USD 84m raise. A focused AU/NZ play with AISF distribution and Xero/MYOB depth has a 12–18 month window before Steelhead localises seriously.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Strong (~85%+). Core SaaS workflow is CRUD + integrations. AI vision QA add-on incurs inference cost but is opt-in tier. Optional hardware (label printers, QR scanners) is owned by the customer. No SMS/voice/human-in-loop dependencies in core product.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Moderate. Many bureaus are single-site; ~15–20% have 2 sites. Larger architectural coaters (Vertikote, AAF) run 3–5 sites — these are aspirational big-fish customers driving expansion ARPU.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Low-to-moderate. Once batch ticket and cert data is in the system, switching is painful. Risk: shop closure (industry contracting ~2.6%/yr per IBISWorld), founder retirement. Expected gross churn 6–10%/yr.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: At AUD 400/mo blended: ~210 customers for AUD 1m ARR. AU TAM ~900–1,200 shops → 20–25% penetration needed; ambitious but plausible given concentrated AISF distribution. Adding NZ + early UK/CA expansion raises ceiling materially.
